rule: `macro`: a macro invocation (C/C++/ObjC function-like macros, Rust `name!`). Calls written inside macro arguments are separate ordinary edges. **C / Objective-C**: function-like macros → call_type macro (high if `#define`d in the scan). C functions bare; **medium**: the callee is named statically (Type.m(), module.f(), an import, `self.m()` inherited from a base outside the scan, an external library type) but is not defined in the scan.
source: KNOWN_GAP: cpp: out-of-scan function-like macros are tagged direct, not macro
notes: assert is a function-like macro (the C/C++ standards specify it as one) defined in <cassert>, outside the scan: call_type macro, and since it is named statically but not defined in the scan, medium — the same treatment SPEC gives the out-of-scan gtest assertion macros (Decisions 2026-11-09: 'function-like macros: macro, medium'). CHECK_POSITIVE is #defined in the scan: macro, high. Macros are preprocessor names, never namespace-qualified, even when invoked inside namespace guard. validate(v) inside the macro arguments are separate ordinary edges.
